{{short description|Mathematical technique in algebraic geometry}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], '''dévissage''' is a technique introduced by [[Alexander Grothendieck]] for proving statements about [[coherent sheaf|coherent sheaves]] on [[Noetherian scheme]]s. Dévissage is an adaptation of a certain kind of [[Noetherian induction]]. It has many applications, including the proof of [[generic flatness]] and the proof that higher [[Direct image functor|direct images]] of coherent sheaves under proper [[morphisms]] are coherent.

Laurent Gruson and [[Michel Raynaud]] extended this concept to the relative situation, that is, to the situation where the scheme under consideration is not necessarily noetherian, but instead admits a finitely presented morphism to another scheme. They did this by defining an object called a relative dévissage which is well-suited to certain kinds of inductive arguments. They used this technique to give a new criterion for a [[module (mathematics)|module]] to be [[flat module|flat]]. As a consequence, they were able to simplify and generalize the results of EGA IV 11 on [[descent (category theory)|descent]] of flatness.<ref>{{harvnb|Gruson|Raynaud|1971|p=1}}</ref>

The word ''dévissage'' is French for ''unscrewing''.

== Grothendieck's dévissage theorem ==
Let ''X'' be a noetherian scheme. Let '''C''' be a collection of objects of the category of coherent ''O''<sub>''X''</sub>-modules which contains the zero sheaf and which has the property that, for any short exact sequence <math>0 \to A' \to A \to A'' \to 0</math> of coherent sheaves, if two of ''A'', ''A''&prime;, and ''A''&prime;&prime; are in '''C''', then so is the third.  Let ''X''&prime; be a closed subspace of the underlying [[topological space]] of ''X''. Suppose that for every irreducible closed subset ''Y'' of ''X''&prime;, there exists a coherent sheaf ''G'' in '''C''' whose fiber at the [[generic point]] ''y'' of ''Y'' is a one-dimensional [[vector space]] over the [[residue field]] ''k''(''y''). Then every coherent ''O''<sub>''X''</sub>-module whose support is contained in ''X''&prime; is contained in '''C'''.<ref>EGA III, Théorème 3.1.2</ref>

In the particular case that {{nowrap|''X''&prime; {{=}} ''X''}}, the theorem says that '''C''' is the category of coherent ''O''<sub>''X''</sub>-modules. This is the setting in which the theorem is most often applied, but the statement above makes it possible to prove the theorem by noetherian induction.

A variation on the theorem is that if every direct factor of an object in '''C''' is again in '''C''', then the condition that the fiber of ''G'' at ''x'' be one-dimensional can be replaced by the condition that the fiber is non-zero.<ref>EGA III, Corollaire 3.1.3</ref>

== Gruson and Raynaud's relative dévissages ==
Suppose that {{nowrap|f : ''X'' &rarr; ''S''}} is a finitely presented morphism of affine schemes, ''s'' is a point of ''S'', and ''M'' is a finite type ''O''<sub>''X''</sub>-module.  If ''n'' is a [[natural number]], then Gruson and Raynaud define an '''''S''-dévissage in dimension ''n''''' to consist of:
# A closed finitely presented subscheme ''X''&prime; of ''X'' containing the closed subscheme defined by the annihilator of ''M'' and such that the dimension of {{nowrap|''X''&prime; &cap; f<sup>&minus;1</sup>(''s'')}} is less than or equal to ''n''.
# A scheme ''T'' and a factorization {{nowrap|''X''&prime; &rarr; ''T'' &rarr; ''S''}} of the restriction of ''f'' to ''X''&prime; such that {{nowrap|''X''&prime; &rarr; ''T''}} is a [[finite morphism]] and {{nowrap|''T'' &rarr; ''S''}} is a smooth affine morphism with geometrically integral fibers of dimension ''n''. Denote the generic point of {{nowrap|''T'' &times;<sub>''S''</sub> ''k''(''s'')}} by τ and the pushforward of ''M'' to ''T'' by ''N''.
# A free finite type ''O''<sub>''T''</sub>-module ''L'' and a homomorphism {{nowrap|&alpha; : ''L'' &rarr; ''N''}} such that {{nowrap|&alpha; &otimes; ''k''(&tau;)}} is bijective.
If ''n''<sub>1</sub>, ''n''<sub>2</sub>, ..., ''n''<sub>''r''</sub> is a strictly decreasing sequence of natural numbers, then an ''S''-dévissage in dimensions ''n''<sub>1</sub>, ''n''<sub>2</sub>, ..., ''n''<sub>''r''</sub> is defined recursively as:
# An ''S''-dévissage in dimension ''n''<sub>1</sub>. Denote the [[cokernel]] of α by ''P''<sub>1</sub>.
# An ''S''-dévissage in dimensions ''n''<sub>2</sub>, ..., ''n''<sub>''r''</sub> of ''P''<sub>1</sub>.
The dévissage is said to lie between dimensions ''n''<sub>1</sub> and ''n''<sub>''r''</sub>. ''r'' is called the '''length''' of the dévissage. The last step of the recursion consists of a dévissage in dimension ''n''<sub>''r''</sub> which includes a morphism {{nowrap|&alpha;<sub>''r''</sub> : ''L''<sub>''r''</sub> &rarr; ''N''<sub>''r''</sub>}}. Denote the cokernel of this morphism by ''P''<sub>''r''</sub>. The dévissage is called '''total''' if ''P''<sub>''r''</sub> is zero.<ref>{{Harvnb|Gruson|Raynaud|1971|pp=7&ndash;8}}</ref>

Gruson and Raynaud prove in wide generality that locally, dévissages always exist. Specifically, let {{nowrap|''f'' : (''X'', ''x'') &rarr; (''S'', ''s'')}} be a finitely presented morphism of pointed schemes and ''M'' be an ''O''<sub>''X''</sub>-module of finite type whose fiber at ''x'' is non-zero. Set ''n'' equal to the dimension of {{nowrap|''M'' &otimes; ''k''(''s'')}} and ''r'' to the codepth of ''M'' at ''s'', that is, to {{nowrap|''n'' &minus; depth(''M'' &otimes; ''k''(''s''))}}.<ref>EGA 0<sub>IV</sub>, Définition 16.4.9</ref> Then there exist affine étale neighborhoods ''X''&prime; of ''x'' and ''S''&prime; of ''s'', together with points ''x''&prime; and ''s''&prime; lifting ''x'' and ''s'', such that the residue field extensions {{nowrap|''k''(''x'') &rarr; ''k''(''x''&prime;)}} and {{nowrap|''k''(''s'') &rarr; ''k''(''s''&prime;)}} are trivial, the map {{nowrap|''X''&prime; &rarr; ''S''}} factors through ''S''&prime;, this factorization sends ''x''&prime; to ''s''&prime;, and that the pullback of ''M'' to ''X''&prime; admits a total ''S''&prime;-dévissage at ''x''&prime; in dimensions between ''n'' and {{nowrap|''n'' &minus; ''r''}}.
